sentences.text: Hello everyone. Welcome back to English for everyday life with me and Molly. Do you love
going to the theater? Maybe you want to watch a play, but you're not sure how to speak English
when you're at the theater. In today's episode, I'll teach you how to speak English at the
theater, whether you are buying tickets, asking about a show, or discussing the performance. This
episode is for A1 level English learners, so I will speak slowly and clearly. By the end of this
episode, you will learn how to buy tickets for a theater show, how to ask for information about
the play, how to talk about seats and locations, how to discuss the play, and give your opinion.
Useful phrases to use before, during, and after the show. So let's get started. One, buying tickets
for the theater. When you go to the theater, the first thing you need to do is buy tickets.
Common phrases. Hi. I would like to buy a ticket for the play. Please. How much are the tickets?
What time does the play start? Are there any discounts for students? Can I buy a ticket online?
Is there a ticket for standing room only? I'd like to sit in the front row please.

The importance of theater etiquette. It's important to follow some theater etiquette to ensure everyone
has a good experience. Important etiquette. Arrive early so you can find your seat before the show
starts. Turn off your phone and keep it silent. Be quiet during the show. Don't talk loudly.
Don't take photos or videos during the performance. Don't leave early, especially if you have tickets
for the entire performance. Respect the actors and other audience members. Clap at the end of the show
if you enjoyed it. Tip. If you're unsure about theater etiquette, just follow the audience.
They usually know when to clap or when to be silent.
